intent: elementwise operation over arrays sharing an index space
note: Write `A + B`, or `method_for(zip(A, B)) <@> f` for a custom kernel. `method_for(zip(A, B))` co-iterates; `method_for(A, B)` is the OUTER PRODUCT — confusing them silently changes the output rank.

intent: all-pairs / outer product / broadcast between two arrays
note: Bracketed operators `A [+] B` / `A [*] B` build the rank-(r+s) outer result; `method_for(A, B) <@> f` does the same with your own kernel. Never nest loops for this.

intent: reduce / fold an array to a scalar, or peel one axis
note: Rank 1: `reduce(A, (+))`. Rank k to a scalar: `reduce(A, (+), axes = k)`. A BARE `reduce` on rank >= 2 defaults to axes = 1 — it peels the innermost axis and returns an array, not a scalar. reduce folds right-to-left, which matters the moment your kernel is not commutative.

intent: several statistics in one pass over the data
note: Fuse the kernels into one loop object and destructure the result: `let (s, ss, n) = reduce((L <@> k_id) <&!> (L <@> square) <&!> (L <@> k_one), (+))`. One traversal, three accumulators, no mutation.

intent: filter rows / WHERE clause / select a subset
note: `mask(xs, pred)` builds the predicate, `compound(data, mask)` applies it; compose masks with `&&` / `||`. There is no filter loop.

intent: stencil, sliding window, lags, finite differences
note: `method_for(halo<I, [-1, 0, 1]>) <@> lambda(w) -> A(w(1)) - A(w(-1))`. The halo carries the offsets, so there is no index arithmetic and no edge guards to get wrong. Only `w(o)` offsets declared in the halo are in scope.

intent: generate an index range instead of materializing iota
note: `range<Idx<8>>` is a virtual array — it costs nothing to iterate and its extents fold at compile time. Map over it with `method_for(range<...>) <@> lambda(i) -> ...`.

intent: pipeline of stages, composing transformations lazily
note: Compose values, not calls: `let stage = object_for(f) >>@ object_for(g)`, apply with `<@>`, materialize with `|> compute`. Nothing runs until compute, so no per-stage temporaries.

intent: running state, recurrence, time stepping, dynamic programming
note: `let rec x: Array<Float like Step> = match x with | zero -> zero | prefix :: n -> prefix :: f(prefix(n - 1))`. This is the replacement for `let mut` + a loop: one pre-allocated buffer, no recursion frames. Reads past the built prefix are implicitly zero, so lag schemes need NO bounds guards.

intent: symmetric pairwise statistics: covariance, comoments, gram matrices
note: Declare `where comm(a, b)` and let the compiler derive triangular storage and iteration (r! savings). `reynolds(g)` MANUFACTURES a commutative kernel by symmetrization when you cannot annotate one. Symmetric output storage is licensed only when the SAME array occupies the commuting positions.

intent: one function that works at several ranks (arity polymorphism)
note: A function typechecks and compiles differently depending on how many array arguments it receives; output rank and symmetry are deduced per call shape. Abstract types are `T^r`; arrays have concrete `Array<T like I, J>` types.

intent: named index types, bounds safety, transposes and reshapes
note: Index types are the type system's spine: `Nat<LatIdx>` and `Nat<LonIdx>` do not unify even at equal extent, which is what makes `A(i)` bounds-safe by construction. `()` is application/indexing (curried); `[]` is ONLY tuple/pack access.

intent: units of measure and dimensional safety
note: `Unit meters` / `Unit mps = meters / seconds`, then `type Speed = Float<mps>`. A unit clash is a refusal, not a warning — fix the declaration rather than casting around it.

intent: group by a key and aggregate per group
note: Group-by is a relational operator over an Idx or EnumIdx key; the group axis becomes part of the result's type.

intent: build a new leading axis by stacking or joining arrays
note: `stack` creates a fresh leading axis; `join` extends one. Off-axis extent disagreement is refused (BL3016) rather than silently truncated.

intent: return several values at once / tuples and packs
note: `let (a, b, c) = ...` destructures; `t[0]` indexes a TUPLE (square brackets are never array indexing).

intent: compile-time constants and compile-time evaluation
note: `let static n = 4` is immutable everywhere and usable as an extent; `static function`s run at compile time and MAY mutually recurse (runtime functions may not — BL2001).

intent: I want a for loop / while loop / imperative iteration
note: The imperative loop was REMOVED from the language and is diagnosed (BL1003) — do not reintroduce it through workarounds. Parallel structure is a loop object (`method_for`/`object_for`); sequential structure is a recursive array (`let rec`). There is nothing else, by design.

intent: probabilistic moments, comoments, distributions
note: The ppl surface provides moment/comoment formers; order-2 formers route to `gram(A, A)` so they inherit BLAS.

intent: plot or emit a rich display frame
note: `import plot` from the stdlib; display frames ride the eval response and appear as image content in blade_eval.
